title: Review: a visit to the office

sections.heading: Quick review
sections.note: Say each phrase aloud before you hear the English.

sections.heading: Dialogue

lines.ar: صَبَاحَ الْخَيْرِ يَا رِضْوَانُ، كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟
lines.en: Good morning, Ridhwan. How are you?
Good morning. Fine, praise be to Allah.

lines.ar: نَعَمْ. وَهٰذِهِ زَمِيلَتِي فَاطِمَةُ، هِيَ مُصَمِّمَةٌ.
lines.en: Yes. And this is my colleague Fatima. She's a designer.
Her office is over there, and her computer is on the table.

lines.ar: لَا، أَشْرَبُ الْقَهْوَةَ. وَكَيْفَ أَخُوكَ يُوسُفُ؟
lines.en: No, I drink coffee. And how is your brother Yusuf?

lines.ar: أَخِي بِخَيْرٍ. هُوَ طَالِبٌ فِي لَاغُوسَ.
lines.en: My brother is fine. He's a student in Lagos.

sections.note: Listen, then read it aloud. Play both roles. Review day: a friend visits Ridhwan at the office. Everything here comes from lessons one to six.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.note: No new grammar today. Let's recap the possessive endings: ee for my, ka for your to a man, ki for your to a woman, hu for his, and haa for her.

sections.heading: Word builder: the root daal, raa, seen, meaning studying

lines.en: a school, the place of studying
studied, or well thought out, the thing that is studied

sections.note: No new pattern today, just patterns you know. Daaris uses faa-il, the doer. Madrasa is maf-al, the place, with the feminine ending. Madroos is maf-ool, the thing done to.

sections.heading: Speak it

lines.en: Do you sometimes work at home?
Model answer: Yes, sometimes I work at home.
Model answer: His office is over there, in the company.
What do you read in the morning?
Model answer: I read the news, then I work.

sections.note: Answer each question aloud about yourself. Then listen to the model answer.
